tools.name: start_book
tools.description: Starts a book of voice, video and written messages for one person, and returns the single link the organiser sends to everyone taking part. Gathering is free and the people recording need no app and no account. Use this as soon as somebody wants to collect messages from a group for one person, wheth

tools.name: get_links
tools.description: Returns the link to forward to contributors, the link that plays every message straight through, and a short message the organiser can paste alongside.

tools.name: add_people
tools.description: Records who is expected to record. Somebody with an email address can be written to by send_it_out and reminded by chase_the_missing; somebody with only a name is reached in a group chat and their name is what the chase reads out. Adding a person sends nothing on its own.

tools.name: send_it_out
tools.description: Emails the invitation once to every person added with an address, and hands back a tap that opens WhatsApp, a text or a mail draft with the message and the link already written, for the family group and for anyone with no address. Nobody is written to twice by this tool.

tools.name: chase_the_missing
tools.description: Works out who is still out, emails a reminder to the ones with an address, and hands back a message naming them, ready for the group chat and ready for one person. A person gets at most one reminder a day and three in all, and never one after they have asked to stop.

tools.name: book_status
tools.description: Returns who is in with their name and relationship, how many voices, videos and written messages have landed, how many carried a photo, who the organiser is still waiting on, and the days left before collecting stops.

tools.name: find_my_book
tools.description: Call it with the email address the book belongs to and Chorus sends that address a six digit code, returning nothing about the books. Call it again with the address and the code and it hands back every book on that account with its handle. Holding the mailbox is the proof, so a book cannot be found

tools.name: change_the_book
tools.description: Changes the settings the organiser can change on the site: the day collecting stops, the questions people are asked, whether they may send voice, video or writing, and which one the button offers first. Nobody is told about a change.

tools.name: their_own_link
tools.description: Returns the second link, which asks the person the book is for about their own life rather than about somebody else. It refuses on a memorial, a new baby and an as they grow book, where the person cannot answer, and it is never the link to put in a group chat.

tools.name: read_the_messages
tools.description: Returns every message with who left it and what they said. A written message reads back whatever was paid; a voice or a video is written out on the tier that includes the words, and where it is not, the tool says so rather than half-answering.

tools.name: close_collecting
tools.description: Stops new messages arriving and returns the final counts with the gift link. Nothing is deleted and nothing is finished; it can be reopened.

tools.name: reopen_collecting
tools.description: Reopens a book that was closed or whose date ran out, and returns the collecting link to send round again.

tools.name: order
tools.description: Returns a payment link for one of the three ways to keep the book: voices, book, or keepsake, which is the printed hardcover. Stripe shows the price and takes the card and, on the keepsake, the postal address. This tool never takes a card and never names a price. Read the prices from https://chorusk

tools.name: order_status
tools.description: Returns whether the book has been paid for and which option was bought, and on a printed one the stage the printer is at with the tracking.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_links, read_the_messages · Private data: add_people · Public sink: get_links, add_people, send_it_out, find_my_book, change_the_book, reopen_collecting.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_links, read_the_messages · Private data: add_people · Public sink: get_links, add_people, send_it_out, find_my_book, change_the_book, reopen_collecting

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
